openings.claim: Make return position depend on fixed face datums and insertion stops, with clamping applied after seating. The nearest rival is that tighter enclosure alone improves return accuracy; the awkward trials do not establish either explanation.
openings.delta: Within the 90 mm joint envelope, cut plywood into two connected corner saddles with captured end-stop offcuts and captive clamp yokes. Allocate four bolts to saddle/carrier/stop fastening and four to the yokes. Recess nuts and retain yokes and fasteners with the supplied cord/loops. Hand-open each yoke without dismantling the carrier, seat the rod against two faces and its stop, then tighten. Preserve the frame angle established at the marked pointer position.
openings.prediction: If inconsistent seating explains the tight-fit penalty, seating before clamping should produce fewer target misses than inserting under partial clamp pressure, despite identical final tightening. The 18 mm substitution should still reach the same datums after adjustment. Persistent misses despite verified seating, or load drift above the target boundary, defeat the proposed repeatability or restraint mechanism.
openings.probe: First check bolt reach, captive retention, saddle rigidity and full opening within the envelope using the available hardware. Fabricate within 100 minutes only if those checks succeed. Compare two procedural configurations on the same joint: seat-then-clamp and insert-under-partial-clamp. Each gets five exchanges of each original rod, then two exchanges replacing the 19 mm rod with 18 mm. Log elapsed exchange time and target return; apply 10 N for ten seconds initially and after exchanges 9, 10 and 12. Record seating gaps and loaded pointer movement. Twenty minutes leaves only 160 seconds for logging/reset if exchanges approach forty seconds; abandon the comparison as inconclusive if overhead cannot fit.
assumptions: Unspecified bolt lengths permit the proposed plywood stack and yokes.
Six pieces provide adequate captured stop material and stiffness; cord/loops suffice for retention.
Hand tightening supplies sufficient restraint without damaging or marking rods.
Actual fabrication and measurement overhead fit the supplied time budgets.

assessment: A bounded prototype probe, with capacity and construction unresolved. No supplied observation establishes success under load, exchange timing, retention or replacement-rod tolerance; deployment requires those checks to pass.
